chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Saʿd ibn Bakr, from Ḥabīb al-Khathʿamī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: When a man sits for the tashahhud and praises Allah, that suffices him.

So the proper way to understand this report is taqiyyah, because it is the view of many among the common people, and we have already explained the obligation of the two testimonies and salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him; it fulfilled the minimum requirement
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony formula recited in salat (prayer) while sitting
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity due to circumstances
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies of faith required in tashahhud
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ: invoking blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.فَحَمِدَ: he praised; here, praising Allah in the sitting of tashahhud

ai.seo_question: Is it sufficient to praise Allah alone in the tashahhud, or are the two testimonies and salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم obligatory?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling of tashahhud in salat (prayer) and mentions a narration indicating that praising Allah alone would suffice. The compiler then clarifies that this report is to be understood as taqiyyah, while the established ruling is the obligation of the two testimonies and salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in the tashahhud.
